title: Accumulator
body:
Internal change
***x++***
assigns, then increments

***x++***
increments then assigns

***x += 5***

> The second heading should read **`++x`**, not `x++`; the description under it is right.
> Post-increment `x++` yields the old value and then increments; pre-increment `++x`
> increments and then yields the new value. Left as written rather than edited, see the
> vault ledger.

---

An accumulator is a [[Variable]] that carries a running result across the passes of a loop.
Two kinds, and each has an initial value you cannot get wrong:

| Job | Start at | Update |
|---|---|---|
| Sum | `0` | `total += x;` |
| Product | `1` | `product *= x;` |
| Count | `0` | `count++;` |
| Running max | the first element, or the type's minimum | `if (x > best) best = x;` |

```c++
int total = 0;
for (int i = 0; i < SIZE; i++)
	total += num[i];

double average = (double)total / SIZE;   // cast, or it truncates
```

Starting a sum at 1 or a product at 0 is the classic [[Logic Errors|logic error]]: it compiles,
runs, and is quietly off by exactly one term. So is priming it inside the loop instead of
before it, which resets it every pass.

The average line is the other one. Two [[Integer]]s divide as integers no matter what the
result is assigned to; see [[Type casting]] and [[Division Algorithm]].

Where the accumulator gets initialised and where it gets updated are two of the seven questions
in [[Loop design]], and they are the two people skip.
